BiblicalUsage: Thou shalt make his pans to receive his ashes, and his shovels, and his basons, and his fleshhooks, says the Lord of the altar, and the vessels of the altar were carried with their shovels and censers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shovel belongs to the holy work because the altar had ashes to clear: the same hands that offered the sacrifice carried the shovel, and no part of the service was beneath the vessels God commanded.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
